arcs.title: Erdős discrepancy problem resolution (Tao, 2015)
arcs.description: Erdős conjectured (1932): for any ±1 sequence x_1, x_2, ... and any C, there exist d, n such that |x_d + x_{2d} + ... + x_{nd}| > C. The polymath project (Gowers, 2010) reduced this to the Elliott conjecture. Tao (2015) proved Elliott using an entropy decrement argument from his Liouville function work. Three components: a multiplicative-function decrement bound, an ergodic-theoretic structure theorem for completely multiplicative functions, a finite-energy argument tying structure theorem to discrepancy. Small-step combinatorial reductions, careful amplification of entropy decrement, gluing discrete and continuous estimates.

arcs.title: Green-Tao theorem (primes in arithmetic progression, 2004)
arcs.description: Green and Tao proved primes contain arithmetic progressions of every length k. Combinatorial transference: Szemerédi's theorem on dense subsets of integers extended to subsets of a 'pseudorandom' set, then primes shown to sit inside a pseudorandom envelope (W-trick + von Mangoldt λ-function). Define pseudorandomness via correlation conditions; construct majorant function for prime density; transfer Szemerédi from dense integer subsets to dense pseudorandom subsets; remove small primes by sifting. Most load borne by combinatorial estimates, not new objects.

arcs.title: Hales-Jewett density via polymath1 (Gowers, 2009)
arcs.description: Density Hales-Jewett (Furstenberg-Katznelson 1991): any positive-density subset of [k]^n contains a combinatorial line for n large. Original proof used ergodic theory and was long. Polymath1 (Gowers 2009) found purely combinatorial proof. Energy-increment iteration in Szemerédi-regularity spirit, partition regularity for the increment step, reduction to dense subset of IP-rich set, finite combinatorial gluing. Polymath produced moves through public blog with Gowers as moderator. Mathematical core was a sequence of specific combinatorial estimates rather than a new framework.

arcs.title: Szemerédi regularity lemma + triangle removal (1975-78)
arcs.description: Every dense graph admits partition into approximately equal parts where almost all pairs are pseudorandom (regular). Triangle removal: graph with o(n^3) triangles can be made triangle-free by removing o(n^2) edges. Iterative refinement: trivial partition, find regular refinement using mean-square energy as potential function, bound iteration by tower-of-twos. Triangle removal followed from regularity by counting triangle-containing edges. Applied to Roth, Behrend, Ramsey, additive combinatorics. Combinatorial estimates, not new objects.

arcs.title: Roth's theorem on 3-term APs in dense subsets (1953)
arcs.description: Roth proved: any subset of {1..N} with density ≥ C / log log N contains a 3-term arithmetic progression. Method: Fourier analysis. If A has density α, write 1_A as α + f where f has small mean. Number of 3-APs in A is α^3 N^2 + (corrections involving Fourier coefficients of f). If A has no 3-APs, the Fourier corrections must absorb the main term, forcing some Fourier coefficient of 1_A to be large; this means A concentrates on an arithmetic progression. Iterate: pass to denser subset on a sub-progression, get density-increment, recurse. Iteration terminates because density is bounded by 1.

arcs.title: Behrend's construction of dense AP-free sets (1946)
arcs.description: Behrend constructed subsets of {1..N} of density 1/exp(O(√log N)) containing no 3-AP — much denser than the trivial 1/3 lower bound and showing Roth's theorem cannot be improved beyond a polynomial-of-log factor. Construction: lift integers to Z^d via base-d expansion; consider points whose coordinates have fixed Euclidean norm (a sphere in Z^d); spheres are AP-free in Z^d and project to dense AP-free subsets of integers. Optimization over d gives the exponential density. Construction is geometric, applied via specific integer-arithmetic embedding.

arcs.title: Furstenberg's ergodic proof of Szemerédi (1977)
arcs.description: Szemerédi's theorem: any positive-density subset of integers contains k-term APs for every k. Furstenberg's correspondence: density-A statements about integer subsets correspond to multiple-recurrence statements about measure-preserving systems. Reduces Szemerédi to proving SZ ergodic theorem: for any measure-preserving T and measurable A with μ(A) > 0, lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ μ(A ∩ T^{-n}A ∩ ... ∩ T^{-(k-1)n}A) > 0. Furstenberg structure theorem: any system decomposes as a tower of compact and weak-mixing extensions. SZ ergodic theorem proved by induction on tower height. Different machinery (ergodic theory, structure theorems) than original combinatorial proof.

arcs.title: Ramsey theory and Erdős-Szekeres (1935 onwards)
arcs.description: Ramsey's theorem (1930): any 2-coloring of edges of large enough complete graph contains monochromatic complete subgraph of any fixed size. Erdős-Szekeres (1935): among any sufficiently many points in general position, some k of them form a convex polygon. Both proofs combinatorial: pigeonhole at scale, induction on depth, careful counting of color/orientation patterns. Erdős reformulated as 'happy ending problem' about 4-points in convex position. Quantitative bounds: r(k,k) ~ 2^k upper, r(k,k) ≥ 2^{k/2} lower (Erdős probabilistic method 1947). Methods: pigeonhole, induction, probabilistic arguments, double-counting, extremal constructions. Specific named problems with combinatorial proofs.
